subject: ODEs allowing empty solution times array?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ODEs allowing empty solution times array?
parts:
May I change the ODE behavior so that it returns an empty array
when the requested solution times array is empty? Currently it
requires the solution times array to be non-empty.

- Bob


> On May 5, 2016, at 2:33 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Bob,
>
> Thanks. The next things after that are to change integrate_ode_cvode to integrate_ode_bdf. We don't need to deprecate that because it didn't exist in any tagged version.
>
> Re: ostream*. I think the right thing to do is to move that up in the argument list. In the way we use it, it's always generated. We could make it a required reference, but we'd have to do a lot of work to propagate that through. I'm just not up to it right now to tackle that.
>
> My head's really fuzzy right now.
>
>
> Daniel
>
>
>
> On Thu, May 5, 2016 at 1:33 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> OK, I'll take a look. I don't see that any of these
> things are major issues.
>
> Is there a reason that ostream* has to be an optional
> pointer argument rather than a required reference?
>
> - Bob
>
> > On May 5, 2016, at 12:39 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> >
> > Hi Bob,
> >
> > If you've got some time to code, I think I need an adult. It got more complicated than I had originally intended.
> >
> > There are two sets of changes and I've committed everything to GitHub.
> > For the math library, it's on branch: feature/issue-292-integrate_ode
> > For the stan library, it's on branch: feature/issue-1886-integrate_ode
> >
> >
> > On the math library, I did what we discussed:
> > 1. renamed integrate_ode to integrate_ode_rk45
> > 2. added arguments to integrate_ode_rk45 with defaults:
> > - absolute_tolerance
> > - relative_tolerance
> > - step_size
> > - max_num_steps
> > 3. renamed integrate_ode_cvode to integrate_ode_bdf
> >
> >
> > On the stan library, I did the right thing and added tests first. Here's what I've done so far:
> > 1. [done] add the deprecation warning to integrate_ode. You can test this with:
> > ./runTests.py src/test/unit/lang/parser/integrate_ode_deprecation_test.cpp
> >
> > 2. [stuck] change integrate_ode to call integrate_ode_rk45. The issue is with the default parameters.
> >
> > First, the test:
> > make src/test/test-models/good/integrate_ode_deprecation.hpp-test
> >
> > I swapped out the generator code to just use integrate_ode_rk45 instead, but since there are now default parameter values, this fails.
> > It generates: integrate_ode_rk45(sho_functor__(), y0, t0, ts, theta, x, x_int, pstream__)
> >
> >
> > Options:
> > 1) I change the Math library to have two function overloads. One with the ostream* and the other with the optional arguments then ostream* and we chain the two functions together.
> > 2) Change the order of the math library's integrate_ode_rk45()'s arguments so ostream* is the first default argument.
> > 3) Generate the defaults. (This seems like the worst option).
> >
> >
> > After I figure this out, I realized I don't know how to do overloading in the parser / generator. So... I think I could use help.
> >
> >
> >
> > First off, any thoughts on how to change to math library to be compatible? Should I just change the order of the parameters? We'll need to replace the stream with writers at some point.
> >
> >
> >
> > Daniel
> >
>
>
